title: SDK Starter Catalyst Lab — Telemetry & Guardrails (Draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a working sketch for a compact, low-friction SDK starter called 'Catalyst Lab' aimed at new internal teams and early external adopters. Focus: 1) minimal install/run loop for a chat + embedding flow, 2) example telemetry and cost signals that map to product SLOs, 3) lightweight guardrails/observability patterns so teams can ship without surprise bills or bad outputs.

Audience
Primary: product engineers integrating Redwood API or Private SDK. Secondary: solutions engineers, docs writers, small pilot customers.

Design principles (guides for decisions)
- Minimal friction: first-run should be "install -> auth -> run sample" in under 5 minutes.
- Opinionated defaults: safe batching, sampling telemetry, token caps, and a single recommended retry policy.
- Observable by default: the starter kit emits a small set of telemetry events and local debug traces (no opt-in).
- Easy to extend: patterns must be copy-paste friendly into an app.

Quickstart (developer flow)
1) Install
   - pip/npm: pip install redwood-catalyst or npm i @redwood/catalyst-sdk
2) Authorize
   - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
3) Run sample chat
   - catalyst init --quickstart chat
   - catalyst run sample-chat
   - Expect: a streamed assistant response, a local trace file, and a telemetry ping.
4) Run sample embed + search
   - catalyst run sample-embed --docs ./sample-data
   - Expect: embedding vectors stored in a temp index and a search sample.

Starter CLI commands (sketch)
- catalyst init --template=chat|qa|embed --name=my-first-integration
- catalyst run sample-chat
- catalyst run sample-embed --docs=./examples
- catalyst status (shows recent token usage, last error, sampled traces)

Core SDK patterns included
- SimpleChatClient: single-file client with streaming and structured output parsing.
- SafeEmbed: wrapper that enforces rate limits, batched calls, and vector quantization hint.
- RetryPolicy: exponential backoff with idempotency keys for safety on network errors.
- KV-Cache example: small local prefix cache showing how to store KV cache across requests.

Telemetry and signals (minimal set to ship)
We want signals that map to product and infra concerns while keeping payloads small:
- session.start (sampled 100%) -> when dev runs sample or opens CLI
- request.start (sampled 10%) -> model, seq_len, prompt_id if present, batching info
- request.end (sampled 10%) -> tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, model_variant, success|error
- error.event (sampled 100% for 5xx, 100% for safety failures) -> error_code, stack_hint
- token.cost.estimate (sampled 100% for first-run then 1% steady) -> estimated cost cents
- rollout.signal (sampled 100% when use pinned model versions change)
Notes: Telemetry payloads should avoid PII and customer prompt text. Send prompt hashes or feature counts only.

Local debug traces
- Simple JSON lines trace file written to ~/.catalyst/traces/ with correlation ids.
- When a sampled request fails or exceeds latency target, include a compact stack and the minimal model config.

Guardrails (defaults we recommend)
- Token cap by default: 512 output tokens for sample templates.
- Cost cap: local throttle that prevents requesting more than $5 estimated cost per CLI session unless explicitly overridden.
- Safety filter: a lightweight pattern-matching filter (server-side/SDK-side) that flags high-risk categories and raises a soft warning; optionally blocks in "locked" mode.
- Fallbacks: if the primary model is unavailable, automatically fallback to a compatible smaller model variant with a notice.

Sampling strategy rationale
- 100% sampling for session.start and obvious errors helps us debug onboarding.
- Low steady-state sampling for request-level telemetry keeps costs down but lets us estimate throughput and token economics.

Developer experience checklist (first-run gating)
- [ ] Install completes without post-install manual steps.
- [ ] Auth works and gives a clear error path if credentials are invalid.
- [ ] Chat sample returns within SLO (default 3s for sample prompt).
- [ ] Telemetry appears in the dev dashboard (session + 1 sampled request).
- [ ] Local trace file exists and is parseable.
- [ ] Cost cap prevented runaway usage in a quick stress run.
- [ ] README contains clear next steps to replace sample prompt with app prompt.

Sample pseudocode (Python-ish)
- note: intentionally terse so copy-paste is easy
"""
from redwood_catalyst import SimpleChatClient
client = SimpleChatClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
with client.stream_chat("Write a terse plan for onboarding SDK users") as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text, end='')
"""

Operational considerations for pilots
- Default quotas: pilots get a reduced default quota; include a clear upgrade path in CLI and Console.
- Billing preview: after the first 100 requests show an estimated monthly run-rate in the CLI to surface cost.
- Support link: catalyst support quick link that attaches the trace file and telemetry sample to a ticket template.

Rollout plan (phases)
1) Internal alpha (eng + 2 SE teams): validate install, telemetry, and guardrails (2 weeks)
2) Broad beta (select early customers): add more sample apps and gather qualitative feedback (4 weeks)
3) Public starter release: polished README, one-page cheat sheet, and Console guided flow (2 weeks)

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How opinionated should the sample retry/backoff be compared to the core SDK? (We risk masking real infra issues if too aggressive.)
- Should telemetry include anonymized prompt features (e.g., token histogram) or only hashes? (privacy vs. signal)
- Cost cap default value: $5 per session is a placeholder — need finance input on reasonable defaults.
- Where to host sample indexes for embedding demos? Local only vs. a short-lived cloud-hosted vector store?

Next steps (actionable)
- Omar: prototype the CLI status command and basic token/cost preview (owner: Omar, due: 2024-10-10)
- Priya: write the safety filter short-list and test it with sample prompts (owner: Priya, due: 2024-10-14)
- Maya: wire up initial telemetry schema and Confluence doc (owner: Maya, due: 2024-10-07)
- Liam: implement local trace writer and attach-to-ticket flow (owner: Liam, due: 2024-10-18)

Appendix: Useful links and refs
- Minimal sample app spec (proto): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter/blob/catalyst/specs/minimal-sample.md
- Infra ticket for fallback routing: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8009
- Example telemetry schema proto (sketch): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVX/Telemetry+Schemas

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally terse; please add copy-paste examples you want to keep in the starter kit rather than references.
- If you disagree with any of the guardrail defaults, note the specific numbers and reasoning in comments below.

End of draft.
